 Judgment

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for death of Sri.Puttaiah, S/o.Late Kariyappa in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 11.10.2019 at around 02.40 p.m., when deceased was riding his Two Wheeler bearing Regn.No.KA-06-EJ-5660 on the left side Kunigal - Tumkur Road from SSIT College side towards Sadashivanagara side, while so going on the left side of said road Near SBI Bank, Sadashivanagara Branch, Tumkur Town, at that time the rider of one Activa bearing Regn.No.KA-06- HA-4913 ridden by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased from back side.

Due to which deceased sustained fatal injuries and died on spot and thereafter the body was shifted to District Hospital, Tumkur and postmortem was conducted and later body was handed over to petitioners to perform funeral rites and they have spent Rs.75,000/- towards cremation and funeral ceremonies.
Prior to accident, he was hale and healthy and was doing Mason, constructing building and agricultural work and earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.

Due to untimely death of deceased,
petitioners life has become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
The accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent riding of said motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents being owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.

3. In pursuance of notice, both respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
2 respective counsels and filed their separate written statement.
4. In objection, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
Se has also denied age, occupation and income of deceased.
Se has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that she is RC owner of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HA-4913, the respondent No.2 is insurer of said vehicle and policy was in force and the rider of offending bike is also having a valid driving license at the time of alleged accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. The 2nd respondent in his written statement has stated that there is dispute regarding issuance of insurance policy in favor of 1st respondent in respect of motor cycle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the alleged accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.

Further the alleged accident occurred because of sole negligence on the part of deceased who was riding his motor cycle with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and lost balance and fell down and there is no nexus between the alleged accident.
Further contended that at the time of alleged accident the insured motor cycle was being rode by one Mohammed Haroon who is a minor.
Further the deceased who was proceeding on motor cycle without wearing helmet.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the husband of 1st petitioner and father of petitioner No.2 to 4 namely Puttaiah succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 11.10.2019 at about 2.40 p.m., Opposite SBI Bank,
Kunigal Road, Sadashivanagara, Tumakuru Town, when he was riding a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-EJ-5660, due to the rash and negligent riding of the Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-06-HA-4913 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
7. The petitioners in support of their case, the petitioner No.4/son of deceased examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.29 and closed his side of evidence.

On the other hand,
Dr.Suresh Babu, the Retired District Surgeon of Tumkur Govt. Hospital summoned and examined as RW.1 and Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas injured in the accident summoned and examined as RW.2 and Sri.G.Suresh, Manager working in respondent No.2 insurance company got examined as RW.3 and Investigator in respondent insurance company by name Sri.H.K.S.Prasanna examined as RW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.10 and closed their side of evidence.

3 8.
I have heard arguments of petitioner and respondent No.2.
Inspite of granting sufficient opportunity respondent No.1 did not address his side of arguments.
Hence, arguments of respondent No.1 taken as heard.
The learned counsel for petitioners filed written arguments.
I have carefully perused the written arguments filed by petitioners.

The learned counsel for petitioners has relied on citations:-
(i) 2017 (1) CCC 166 (SC) in between Bhogireddi Varalakshmi and others Vs. Mani Muthupandi and others.
(ii) 2021 (2) Civil LJ 132 in between New India Assurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Santhosh Kanwar and others.
(iii) 2021 (2) Civil LJ 400 in between New India Assurance Company Ltd., Vs.
Smt.Somwati and others.

The ratio and the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and Hon'ble High Court of Rajasthan in the above judgments are taken into consideration to decide the above case.

9. My answer to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.1:-

In this case the petitioners contend that on 11.10.2019 at about 02.40 p.m., Opp. SBI Bank, Kunigal Road, Sadashivanagara, Tumkur Town on Kunigal - Tumkur Road, the deceased Sri.Puttaiah had met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HA-4913 by its rider and he died on spot.
11.
The petitioner No.4 examined as PW.1 and produced Ex.P.2 and 3 FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.3, petitioner No.4/son of deceased has given first information to police on 11.10.2019.
On the basis of Ex.P.3 police registered a case as per Ex.P.2.
He has stated in his complaint that due to rash and negligent riding of offending motor cycle by its rider the accident occurred.
Ex . P.5
- Crime Detail Form.
After registering case Police went near place of accident and drawn Sketch as per Ex.P.6 by narrating the place of accident.
Ex.P.7 PM Certificate, wherein mentioned that deceased Sri.Puttaiah died due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of injuries sustained.
After investigation police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.4 against rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304-(A) of IPC, U/s.134(A&B), 187 of M.V.Act.

Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
4 12.

The respondent No.1 owner of offending vehicle in her written statement, she has contended that at the time of accident rider was possessing valid driving license and his vehicle insured with respondent No.2.

The respondent No.2 filed written statement, in his written statement contended that the insured Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HA-4913 was rode by one Mr.Mohammed Haroon, who was minor, collusion with the police filed charge sheet against one Mr.Mohammed Yusuf Abbas by swapping the rider with an intention to facilitate the claimants to claim compensation.
In order to prove the contention of respondent insurance company, the insurance company summoned the Dr.Suresh Babu, District Hospital, Tumkur and examined as RW.1.
He has deposed that one Mr.Mohammed Haroon came to hospital and he was conscious and as per hospital document, Mr.Mohammed Haroon himself came to hospital.
Further he has deposed that he himself examined Mr.Mohammed Haroon.
As per Ex.R.1, Mr.Mohammed Haroon was traveling on two wheeler.
The respondent insurance company summoned Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas before the tribunal and examined as RW.2.
He has deposed that he has obtained driving license on 25.06.2020 and after accident he was conscious and he went to Tumkur Government Hospital for treatment.
Further he has admitted Ex.R.1 MLC document belongs to him.
Further RW.2 denied that he was riding two wheeler at the time of accident.
Further he has deposed that his father was riding two wheeler at the time of accident.
On perusal of Ex.R.1, wherein the doctor mentioned that road traffic accident while traveling in two wheeler at about 2.40 p.m., hit by another two wheeler.
Further the respondent insurance company examined its Manager by name Sri.G.Suresh as RW.3.
In his chief examination, he has denied the accident.

Further deposed that as per investigation made by their company as per statement of one eye witness by Sri.Lokesh who was having tea in tea shop near the place of alleged accident stated that the rider of two wheeler came along with a pillion rider and had hit another two wheeler in which Sri.Puttaiah was riding and the age of the rider is between 18-20 years and the age of pillion rider is aged about 20 years who escaped unhurt and he fled the scene after this accident.

Further, he has deposed that Mr.Mohammed Haroon was not holding driving license in order to fasten the liability on the insurance company the owner of Honda Activa who is none other than the mother of Mr.Mohammed Haroon in connivance with her husband Sri.Mohammed Yousuf and the jurisdiction police swapped the name of rider and got the charge sheet filed in the name of Sri.Mohammed Yousuf.
13.

In order to prove his contention, he has produced one C.D. said to be conversation of one Sri.Lokesh, who was said to be witnessed the accident and he has stated that Mr.Mohammed Haroon was riding the motor cycle.
RW.3 in his cross examination deposed that as per investigation report, one Mr.Mohammed Haroon, who was riding the motor cycle.
Further in his cross examination, he has deposed that they have no problem to examine Sri.Lokesh.
Further the insurance company in order to establish that they have recorded the conversation of said eye witness to the incident, they have been examined Sri.H.K.S.Prasanna as RW.4.

He has deposed that he visited the spot of accident and he has made an enquiry at the alleged place of accident and as per statement of eye witness by name Sri.Lokesh, who was having tea at the place of accident stated that the rider of two wheeler came along with pillion rider had hit another two wheeler in which Sri.Puttaiah was riding and the age of rider is between 18-20 years and the age of pillion rider is aged about 20 years who escaped unhurt and he fled the scene after this accident.
Further he deposed that he had recorded the statement of eye witness and same was submitted to the company.

In his cross examination, he has deposed that he himself recorded the video from his mobile phone Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
5 and he has recorded the statement of Sri.Lokesh in Tumkur.
Further he has deposed that he has mentioned the name, address and mobile number of Sri.Lokesh in his chief examination.
But on perusal of chief examination of RW.4 except name he has not stated mobile number and address of Sri.Lokesh.
RW.4 also deposed that they can examine eye witness before the tribunal.
The respondent insurance company produced C.D with sealed cover.

In order to show C.D. is genuine,
they have produced report issued by ICS Assure Services Pvt. Ltd., marked at Ex.R.5.

RW.3 & 4 have deposed that they can examine Sri.Lokesh before the tribunal, but the insurance company not summoned Sri.Lokesh before the tribunal to establish that the voice which is said to be in C.D. is belongs to one Sri.Lokesh.
The conversation which is said to be in C.D., is not confronted to the witness.
Only production of CD before the tribunal is not sufficient.
The insurance company has to examined the Sri.Lokesh before the tribunal to establish the voice which recorded by insurance company is belongs to said Sri.Lokesh and he witness the incident.

Further more only on the basis of conversation said to be recorded by investigator of insurance company, this tribunal cannot come to the conclusion that one Mr.Mohammed Haroon was riding the motor cycle not by his father.

When respondent insurance company has taken specific plea that one Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas was riding the motor cycle at the time of accident, they have to prove by placing sufficient and cogent evidence.
On meticulous perusal of evidence of Rw.1 & 2 the respondent insurance company did not elicit anything to establish Mr.Mohammed Haroon was riding the motor cycle at the time of accident.
Even on perusal of Ex.R.1 - MLC Document, wherein mentioned Mr.Mohammed Haroon was traveling on two wheeler.
But the respondent insurance company not placed sufficient evidence before the tribunal to show that Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas was riding motor cycle at the time of accident.

Only basing upon the so called conversation between the investigation of insurance company and one Sri.Lokesh, this tribunal cannot hold that Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas was riding the vehicle without corroborative evidence.
The I.O. after thorough investigation filed charge sheet before the tribunal.
The I.O. in charge sheet he has stated that one Sri.Mohammed Yusuf Abbas was riding the motor cycle.
The I.O. also recorded the statement of eye witnesses and shown them as charge sheeted witnesses.
The Insurance company not examined the charge sheeted witnesses before the tribunal to prove their contention.
As per Ex.R.1, Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas has sustained injuries and went to hospital.
In Ex.R.1, it is mentioned that he was traveling in two wheeler.
In the said initial document, wherein not stated that he was riding the motor cycle, but only stated that he was traveling in two wheeler.
The respondent insurance company except examining the Manager of Insurance Company and Investigator, they have not tried to examine eye witness before the tribunal.

As per charge sheet, the accident occurred in Tumkur City at about 2.40 p.m. According to Investigator of insurance company at the place of accident, there was a tea shop and when Sri.Lokesh was taking tea he witnessed the incident.
When such being the case, what prevented the insurance company to examine the Sri.Lokesh and other persons who were at the time of accident.
The respondent insurance company has not proved by placing cogent evidence that Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas was riding the motor cycle, just producing C.D before the tribunal is not sufficient.
The respondent insurance company has to prove the contents of Ex.R.3 - C.D before the tribunal.
When respondent insurance company has not proved the contents of Ex.R.3, then only production of Ex.R.3 - C.D before the tribunal is not sufficient to prove their contention.
14. On perusal of sketch prepared by I.O., the accident occurred at junction in daylight.

On meticulous perusal of entire oral and documentary evidence placed by petitioner and respondent,
Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
6
the rider of offending vehicle dashed against the vehicle of deceased.
Further on perusal of entire case record, there is no dispute regarding the accident.

When respondent insurance company not discharged their burden by proving that one Mr.Mohammed Haroon Abbas was riding motor cycle,
then the oral and documentary evidence placed by parties, it establishes that due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending vehicle the accident occurred and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age,
avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., let me discuss one by one;
(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of deceased Sri.Puttaiah is shown as 60 years.

In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.16 & 21 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card and pan card, wherein the date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1955, the accident occurred on 11.10.2019, so the age of deceased was 65 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case '07' multiplier is applicable in present case.

(ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Puttaiah was mason and constructing buildings and doing agricultural work and earning a sum of .40,000/-
per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioners have produced RTC and Order copy of Tahasildar marked at Ex.P.14 & 15.
In order to show income from agriculture, petitioners have not produced any documents.
Case on hand the petitioners have not produced any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2019 at .14,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.
Case on hand the petitioners have not produced any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.
Accordingly, the notional income of deceased during the year 2019 treated as Rs.14,000/- per month.
(iii) In view of Pranaya Sethi and other Case the Hon'be Supreme Court held that more than 60 years of age future prospects is not applicable.
Case on hand deceased was aged about 65 years.
Hence, the petitioners are not entitled for future prospects.

Admittedly deceased Sri.Puttaiah,
married, having wife and children.
On perusal of the cause title of the petition, petitioner No.2 is aged about 30 years, petitioner No.2 aged about 27 years and petitioner No.4 is aged about 25 years.
According to PW.1, petitioner No.2 is married.
But there is no evidence where she is residing and there is no evidence whether she was depending upon income of her father or not.
Hence, she is not considered as a dependent.

Accordingly, petitioner No.1, 3 and 4 were depending upon the income Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
7 of deceased.

So, as per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court in Smt. Saral Verma case where number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.

Thus petitioners are entitled to compensation of .7,83,972/- towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:
 Calculation Total (In R.)
 1/3rd of .14,000/- .9,333/-
 (deduction of .4,667/-)
 .9,333/- multiply by 12 .1,11,996/-
 .1,11,996/- multiply by 07 .7,83,972/-
 Multiplier (B):- Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;
In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India, in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 & in between National insurance company LTD V/s Pranay Sethi and Ors, The petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased Sri.Puttaiah is entitled for .40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and petitioner No.2 to 4 being the children of deceased are entitled for .40,000/- each towards parental consortium and they are also entitled for .15,000/- towards loss of estate and .15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w.
MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:

sentences.text: "However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.
Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
18. This tribunal already held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of Honda Activa bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HA-4913 by its rider.
Even the police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:

For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed with cost.

The petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation of .9,73,972/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Nine Hundred and Seventy Two only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioners No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 40% and Petitioner No.2 to 4 being the children of deceased are entitled for 20% each.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1 to 4, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 4 and remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to their place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
They are entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
9 Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me, in the open Court on this the 21st day of January, 2023.)
(Raghavendra.

opennyai_summary.decision:
19. Issue No.3:
For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed with cost.
The petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation of .9,73,972/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Nine Hundred and Seventy Two only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioners No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 40% and Petitioner No.2 to 4 being the children of deceased are entitled for 20% each.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1 to 4, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 4 and remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to their place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
They are entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Smt.Sharadamma vs Smt.Roshan Ara on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135723245/
9 Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
